 Judgment

The above appeal is filed by the petitioner/claimant seeking to set aside the Judgment and Decree dated 31.08.2023 passed in https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis M.C.O.P.No.33 of 2022 by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal and Thirupattu (Special Sub Judge, Special Court, Thirupattur).

sentences.text: 2. It is the case of the appellant that, on 06.01.2022 at about 12.50 Hours, when the respondent was travelling in a bus bearing Regn.No.TN 23 N 2248 belonging to the appellant Corporation, in order to avoid hitting a two wheeler which was proceeding in front of the appellant Corporation bus, the driver of the Corporation bus had applied sudden brake, due to which the passengers in the bus including the respondent were thrown out of the bus.
Thereby, the respondent / claimant sustained grievous injuries.

Therefore, the appellant had filed a claim petition claiming a sum of Rs.75,000/-

sentences.text: Before the Tribunal, the appellant had examined P.W.1 and P.W.2 and marked Exhibits P.1 to Ex.P.12.
On the side of the respondent, he examined R.W.1 and no document was marked on his behalf.
After adjudication, the Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.30,284/- as compensation to the appellant.
Not satisfied with the same, the appellant https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis has preferred the present appeal seeking enhancement.

4. The learned counsel appearing for the appellant / Transport Corporation submitted that, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the two wheeler, the driver of the appellant Corporation Bus had applied sudden brake, due to which the respondent sustained injuries.

However, the Tribunal without considering the oral and documentary evidence, on the basis of the FIR, had come to a conclusion that the accident had happened solely due to the driver of the appellant Corporation Bus and awarded a compensation of Rs.30,284/- which is per se unsustainable.
Further, FIR is not a conclusive proof nor is an encyclopedia for deciding the case and it is only to set the criminal law in motion and no further.

While so, the mere fact that the FIR has been lodged against the driver of the appellant transport corporation alone cannot be the basis to attribute rash and negligent driving on the driver of the appellant transport corporation.

Moreso,
the claimant / first respondent failed to implead the driver of the two wheeler as party in the claim petition.
When that be so, the appellant Corporation is not liable to pay the compensation in favour of the claimant.
Accordingly, he prayed https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis to allow this appeal.

5. Heard the learned counsel appearing for the appellant and perused the materials available on record.
6.
The factum and manner of the accident is not disputed by the parties.
Therefore, this Court is not entering into the said aspect.
Admittedly, the first respondent is a passenger of the appellant Transport Corporation Bus.

It is the claim of the appellant Corporation that due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the motor cycle which was proceeding in front of the aforesaid bus,
the Driver of the said bus had applied sudden brake, due to which the first respondent / claimant sustained grievous injuries.
As per Section 147(2) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the passengers of public service vehicle are also entitled for compensation.

Hence, the appellant Corporation is liable to indemnify the claimant for the injuries sustained by him and upon taking into consideration the nature of injuries suffered by him and after proper appreciation of the material documents placed before it, the tribunal has awarded the compensation, which cannot be said to be erroneous or https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis arbitrary and, therefore, this Court confirms the award passed by the tribunal in favour of the respondent / claimant.

7. For the reasons aforesaid, this Appeal stands dismissed, confirming the award passed by the tribunal in MCOP.No.33 of 2022 dated 31.08.2023 and the appellant is directed to deposit the compensation of Rs.30,284/- awarded by the tribunal to the credit of MCOP.No.33 of 2022 along with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of deposit and costs as awarded by the Tribunal, less the amount, if any, already deposited, within a period of six weeks (6) from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment, if not already deposited.

On such The Managing Director vs Salam Khan on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127772425/
2 deposit being made, the Tribunal is directed to transfer the said amount to the respondent directly to his bank account through RTGS within a period of two (2) weeks thereafter.
